title: A call of three or more cannot negotiate: the signalling has no way to address a peer, and the capability advertises no limit
design:
Found 2026-11-25, answering Mark's question: what happens when someone
opens a call in a room of 12 -- 12 connections or 12*11?

Neither. Today two parties work and three or more do not connect at all.

WHAT SCALES. The call room is one MLS group: 12 people in the chat gives
a call room with 12 members. The media secret is one per epoch for the
whole room (Agent::media_secret), the same bytes for every member, which
is deliberate (mimid-agent-core::media: "a call among fewer people is a
smaller room, not a smaller key").

WHAT DOES NOT. The signalling carries no recipient, at any layer:

* jmap_vtc_server::CallSignalRequest { signal, sdp, candidate }
* mimid_agent_core::call_signal::CallSignal { kind, sdp }
* mimid_agent_store::Change::CallSignal { room, sender, kind, sdp }
* the VTCCallSignal pushed to clients, which names the SENDER
  (crates/mimid-agent-jmap/src/vtc_stream.rs participant_id)

and Store::send_call_signal(room, kind, sdp) sends one MLS application
message to the whole call room.

So in a call of 12: an offer reaches all 11 others, each answers, and
each answer reaches all 11 including the 10 it was not for. A client can
group INCOMING signals by sender. It cannot say which peer its OWN offer
is for, and a mesh needs one offer per peer because each PeerConnection
has its own DTLS parameters and ICE ufrag. Eleven offers from alice are
indistinguishable to bob. Two parties work because "the other one" is
unambiguous.

THE DRAFT SAYS THE BROADCAST IS INTENTIONAL.
draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00 (~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec, line 1890): a signal
reaching every member of the call's MIMI room is what is wanted "in a
call whose media is peer-to-peer between two participants, or one whose
media passes through a selective forwarding unit that is itself a
participant. In a mesh call among three or more, the session description
a participant intends for one peer is readable by all of them, so such a
call gets no privacy between its own participants from this mechanism
and MUST NOT be presented as though it did."

So the intended shape for 12 is 12 CONNECTIONS, one per client to an SFU
that joins the call as a disclosed key-holding participant and forwards
SFrame-encrypted media it cannot read -- which is what the whole-group
media secret is for, and which is bead mimid-1wgh.114.7, not built. A
mesh would be 11 PeerConnections per client and 66 pairs, and nobody
ships that past about six.

TWO THINGS THAT ARE OURS TO FIX:

1. FOR MARK, mimid's side. crate::vtc::capability advertises
   "maxParticipantsPerCall": null -- the draft defines null as "no
   server-imposed limit" -- while Store::start_call_with invites
   everyone in the parent chat. A client is told it may start a call of
   12, does, and gets silence: no refusal, no warning, no log. The
   options are to advertise 2 until mimid-1wgh.114.7 lands, to advertise
   2 and refuse a larger call room, or to leave it null and say in
   docs/agent.md that a call of three or more needs an SFU the
   deployment supplies. Each is a decision, not a cleanup.

2. wg, the draft's side. The paragraph above treats a mesh call as a
   PRIVACY problem. It is also not CONSTRUCTIBLE: with no way to address
   an offer to one peer, a mesh among three or more cannot complete
   negotiation at all, however little its participants mind reading each
   other's descriptions. Either the paragraph should say so, or
   VTCCall/signal should take an optional target participant id (which
   does not need to hide the signal from the room -- it only needs to
   say whom it is for).

NOT A REGRESSION, and nothing here is broken by beads mimid-1wgh.114.14
or mimid-1wgh.129: it has been this way since the surface was built,
and the surface is off by default (decision mimid-1wgh.119).
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-11-25, as decided.

* crate::vtc::MAX_PARTICIPANTS = 2, and capability() advertises it in
  maxParticipantsPerCall instead of null.
* VtcBackend::create_call counts the parent chat's participants (what
  start_call_with invites, since `among` is None here) and refuses with
  invalidProperties BEFORE hosting the room, so a refused call leaves no
  call room and announces nothing.
* docs/agent.md and crates/mimid-agent-jmap/src/vtc.rs corrected: both
  said maxParticipantsPerCall was null, which this session's earlier
  commit 80eb9e30 had written down as true.

Test: crates/mimid-agent/tests/vtc.rs
a_call_in_a_chat_of_more_than_two_is_refused. Red first, and the red run
showed why the check is worth having: without it the call fails anyway,
but as `forbidden` / "keyMaterial for mimi://a.example/u/carol:
NoConsent" -- a downstream consent error that tells a client nothing
about the real limit.

CLOSING, because what this bead could decide is decided and done. The
underlying limitation -- a call of three or more cannot negotiate,
because a signal reaches every member of the call's room and nothing in
it says which peer it is for -- is not fixed and is not fixable here:
it needs the selective forwarding unit of bead mimid-1wgh.114.7. And
bead mimid-1wgh.131 is what makes the ceiling usable rather than only
honest, since VTCCall/set still cannot say who to call.

The wg half of this bead is not done: draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00's
paragraph on mesh calls says they get no privacy between participants,
and should also say they cannot complete negotiation at all. That is a
one-paragraph change to Mark's own draft and needs his OK.
